text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Mubarak will discuss with Palestinian President Arafat on Wednesday the future of the Middle East peace process after the Hebron agreement. Egypt refuses the division of Sudan and will not intervene in the conflict between the government and the opposition.
- Parliament approves a law allowing foreign and Egyptian investors to set up and operate airports.
- Egypt will privatise water and sewerage companies in February.
- Sudan opposition intensify efforts to take over Damazin.
- Standard & Poors to hold an internet discussion on the Egyptian economy.

- Mubarak holds a ministerial meeting to discuss the Middle East peace process and the situation in Sudan. What is happening in Sudan is an internal conflict between the government and the opposition. Stability will increase Egypt's ability to develop. Our security apparatus is capable of rounding up criminals.
- Five thousand investement projects with a total cost of 79 billion pounds set up last year.
- Transport minister Soleiman Metawalli says international airports will not be privatised.
- Cairo governorate says general transport authority is not responsible for bus which fell off a bridge and killed 39 people.
- Mubarak says Egypt refuses any attempts to partition Sudan.
- Security council will meet to discuss imposing an air embargo on Sudan.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu says that a Palestinian state is a threat to Israel.
- Huge fire guts weaving factory in Cairo
